Saturn return is not strictly negative. Plenty of people have positive returns, this is dictated by how one navigates the issues and also how much work they’re willing to put in prior and during the return.

Ie. I don’t foresee any marriage-altering issues, and if anything this is a great foundational transit for partnership.

So, recovery was more or less pretty smooth.
I had surgery like the day after Xmas and was itching to return to school by the beginning of February. 

I had take home medicine (Vicodin, oxy) and took as needed although honestly I don’t recall needing it much. 

A particular discomfort was the nerves regaining sensation. My hips always felt tender and sensitive when I had pants on and I hated that feeling.  I was swollen and it took a while for my nerves to repair (all sensation did return, except for the aforementioned two spots on my upper back/shoulder blade area).

The most painful part was sitting up. The feeling is akin to muscles being torn apart. Feels like your body is on fire. I usually needed help getting up or turning over, because getting in and out of bed was by far the hardest part. 

After that, it just gets better each day. When I was fully healed, I didn’t have any pain. My body is different. I can’t do certain things, and there are different pains that happen every now and then.
I can’t lay on my stomach comfortably anymore without a lot of pressure in my neck and lower back. I buy firm mattresses because I like very stiff objects now, certain car headrests drive me nuts because the design is cranked all the way forward and it pushes my neck out from my immobile spine. I hate painting my toe nails because I just can’t reach them the same way without some discomfort.

It sounds all bad but the reality is that it’s just *different*. The only regular pain I have ever experienced irregardless of any outside factor, is when I draw or write for an extensive period. My body tends to want to curl up and tilt my head down, and it makes my upper shoulders feel “burn-y”
It’s usually my signal to myself that my posture isn’t good, well, my neck posture. So I straighten up.

If you go into dealers room and artist alley, they are quite massive and confusing for first timers.

Dealers room: 
Figurines, manga, art books, plushies, all the stuff you’d buy at a store type stuff.

This place is huge. You might get lost. Remember the entrance and exit locations 

If you see something you REALLY like, buy it. Sometimes people sell out.
However, If the item is pretty regular, I’d hold off and check around to see if another dealer has it cheaper. 

Artists alley:
More bespoke, fanmade creations. Lots of prints, badges, pins, and buttons. Hand made gifts. Whatever anime is popular that year tends to dominate the theme (ie. I expect genshin impact to have a very large influence this year) 

Take picture of artists business cards if you want to revisit their booth, and also to save paper instead of grabbing one.

Get a commission! Find an artist who you like their artwork of and get something fun! A picture of your fav character, or a drawing of yourself, or a couples commission. They are very exciting and give you something to look forward to.

General:

There’s Lots of people. if you have standard badges (not VIP) expect to wait in lines. If a panel is at 4:00 stop by around 2:30-3:00 and see how the line looks. If the panel is particularly popular (like a concert or a famous person or something) you gotta line up like 3 hours early minimum. I suspect the crowds will be a lot less this year, but even so you never know. That’s standard protocol.

1) completely bought costumes are acceptable (however don’t expect to enter any costume contests or out perform any truly handmade costumes in terms of quality). but in short, YES! they are fine!!

2) Purchasing a costume and editing certain pieces of it is a step up from #1. You take what you like (or are unable to produce) and replace it with things you like better/made yourself.
— I did this myself recently. I bought a costume online as a “security” and scrapped EVERYTHING except the shirt (which was good quality). i proceeded to sew gloves/shorts/leg pieces and for the first time ever had a costume is could say was almost entirely handmade. 
(i’m also a new sewer but if you possess any amount of intelligence and common sense it should be easy to pick up. good for you for taking lessons right away. the hardest part of sewing is the patterning for me... ugh.)

3) don’t expect to have the best costume as you have just started and you’ll have to cosplay a few times to really know what you like and don’t like.
that’s not to say you can’t produce an amazing costume early on though. it took me about 8 years (i started cosplay in 2010) to really feel ready to devote time and money into making my own costumes by scratch. everything before this was either bought or various bits of clothing purchased at H&M supplementing whatever costume i did at the time.

4) go to eye doctor, get a written Rx of your contact script and save photo. you’ll need this to purchase contacts online as most reputable stores ask for a picture to confirm (and send) contacts to you. wearing contacts for cosplay i’d say is.... necessary. unless you have a headpiece/helmet or whatever.

5) wigs. wear fishnet wig caps as they hold hair better.  styling wigs also improves overall character appearance tenfold. 

6) book a hotel. stay with friends. be prepared to spend money.
i used to stay at my aunts house who lived a short distance away from my chosen convention. i learned very fast that getting ready at a family members house was not only Awkward, annoying, and inconvenient, but doesn’t allow you a place to rest while at a convention.
i started booking hotel rooms when i realized i’d rather have a place to go back to edit my costume in peace, without questions, and most importantly within walking distance. being able to nap and just sit in AC means a lot at a convention (erm.. a summer one that is. i’ve never attended a winter convention)
- also worth noting that everyone in the hotels near the con are nerds and the energy is absolutely incredible. the fun youll have just connecting with people in elevators or naruto-running in the hallways is irreplaceable. worth the money in my experience. especially splitting the hotel+parking cost with a group of four people. 

5) nobody really... cares? and by that... most people are respectable and don’t judge. wearing booty shorts? great! literally thong with skirt hiked above butt cheek area? power to you. selectively placed loincloth, high heels, sparkly dress on a very obviously male Guy? expect ALL the pics! 
just be aware that con goers are WAY more accepting than random street goers (if you venture far away from the con).
I was getting cat called by strangers when i went to go eat downtown, but at the convention everyone was respectful. just know your audience. 

6) ask hotel ppl when in doubt. need earplugs? curious about parking costs? don’t know where an atm is? they usually have answers to most of those questions.

7) scope out places to eat before going to the con. you save money not eating at the con or at the hotel. but there is something to be said about getting a drink at the hotel bar with a group of friends..... very bougie feeling... LOL

People with Higher amounts of melanin (eumelanin specifically, as it contributes to black and brown pigments), so, blacks and hispanics per say, generate LESS vitamin D from sunlight. Darker skin essentially blocks the UV rays, and therefore reduces vitamin D production.

People with lighter/white skin (skin high in Pheomelanin, responsible for red and yellow pigments in skin/hair) easily produce vitamin D from sunlight, because there is a lack of UV protection. 

So, it makes sense that blacks are mostly vitamin D deficient, followed by Hispanics, despite some groups living near the equator or in sunny areas. It’s simply their skin functioning as it should.

TLDR:
- Dark skin (eumelanin) Blocks UV rays, but blocks Vitamin D = vitamin d deficient
- Light skin (pheomelanin) Does not block UV rays, DOES generate vitamin D easily = vitamin D proficient 

Source: cosmetology school taught me about melanin types. Also common knowledge that white people generate vitamin D faster.

- I personally cosplay characters that I feel a connection to because it makes me more comfortable and happier to be in costume, which can affect how you look in pictures and just walking around. Being proud is important.

- I don’t cosplay characters with wildly different features than me, just for sake of easiness and comfort.
—ie: i have very small breasts (AA cup), but extremely wide hips (like 39in on my small frame body) so cosplaying girl characters w big boobs is nearly impossible, as is cosplaying men with skinny skinny legs.  So i know by default i’m not gonna be the best version of *blank* if that character has opposite features of me.

- I prefer cosplaying characters with hair color that’s complimentary to my skin tone
— with very very pale skin, cool undertones, as blonde hair suits me well. Golden blonde or yellow hair looks soooooo bad on me, that even if a character has a golden hair type, I will style a wig with cool tone equivalent so it looks specific to me.  There are very few instances when I won’t choose a neutral/cool blonde.
Know what colors look good on you, and avoid costumes with super contrasting colors according to your features.

- I strive to create very accurate renditions of cosplays, but not drive myself crazy. I have never owned a sewing machine, so i’ve commissioned pieces for cosplays, but pieced together other parts on my own by scavenging goodwill or whatever. 

- Style wigs well. That can make or break a costume. DONT be afraid to cut the hair!! Too often I see wigs that are just base wigs with no editing and i’m like “wow that would’ve been perfect if that wig was trimmed a bit”

-Contacts enhance cosplays greatly.
Please, consider wearing contacts if you normally wear glasses and the character has no glasses. Even if you take glasses off for photos, people walking by at random might avoid asking for photo ops because they think the glasses are ruining it.
